messages:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT — Significant latency SLO breach (p95/p99) observed in us-west-2 cluster. Streaming stall rate increased ~30% over baseline. Paging oncall: @Maya (SRE-oncall).

Maya (SRE-oncall): acknowledging. seeing p95 jump from ~120ms to ~2.3s and p99 ~7.8s on streaming routes. Affected shard set: gw-west-2-accel-07..10. Starting triage.

Maya (SRE-oncall): quick telemetry:
- 5m window: p95 = 2.3s, p99 = 7.8s, error rate +1.2% (timeouts), streaming stalls +30% (server-side stalls).
- GPU telemetry: node 07 ECC correctable errors rising, thermal sensors trending 85-92C. NVLink error counters show intermittent spikes.

Ian (eng-runtime): noted. can you dump runtime logs for one noisy session? Also check KV cache hit ratios; streaming stalls often correlate with KV eviction thrash.

Maya (SRE-oncall): grabbing logs. command: ```
$ rctl query metrics --cluster us-west-2 --nodes gw-west-2-accel-07..10 --range 5m --metrics latency_p95,latency_p99,stream_stalls,ecc_correctable_count,gpu_temp
```

Maya (SRE-oncall): pasted snippet from metrics API: ```
{ "node":"gw-west-2-accel-07","p95":2400,"p99":7800,"stream_stalls_pct":32.1,"ecc_corr":142,"gpu_temp_c":89 }
{ "node":"gw-west-2-accel-08","p95":2100,"p99":6500,"stream_stalls_pct":28.6,"ecc_corr":97,"gpu_temp_c":87 }
```

Samira (eng-sre): confirming KV cache eviction spikes for those nodes at the same time window. eviction rate x5. Could be memory pressure from ECC-corrected retries or thermal throttle causing slower processing leading to queue pileups.

Jorge (hw-ops): on the hardware side: ECC correctable error rates above baseline but not outright uncorrectable yet. Thermal readings show rapid rise coincident with load spike. Might be a fan curve/regulator issue on 07. I'll run quick sensor probe and check BMC logs.

Kevin (oncall): advising mitigation: take affected nodes out of serving pool (drain), switch streaming customers to warm pool that has spare capacity, and route long-tail streaming to fallback model variant with lower memory footprint. Can we do this without disrupting queued sessions?

Ian (eng-runtime): actionable plan:
1) Mark gw-west-2-accel-07..10 AS DRAINING in router: ```
$ routerctl set-schedule --drain nodes gw-west-2-accel-07..10 --grace 30s
```
2) Promote warm pool replicas (gw-west-2-warm-*) and increase concurrency there by +20% for streaming routes.
3) Apply runtime patch to reduce per-request batch size and disable aggressive prefetching for streaming endpoints to avoid KV thrash.

Maya (SRE-oncall): executing 1) and 2) now. Router shows in-progress drain — most new connections are moving. Observing tail latency dropping for non-streaming routes.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy to runtime: reduce-prefetch flag toggled on streaming routes (deploy id: dpl-2026-03-17-0912).

Ian (eng-runtime): pushed runtime config: ```
PATCH /runtime/config
{ "streaming": { "prefetch": false, "max_batch_tokens": 512 } }
```

Maya (SRE-oncall): after routing + config changes: p95 down to ~380ms within 2m, p99 trending to ~1.8s, streaming stalls reduced to +8% over baseline. CPU on warm pool up ~12%. No customer-facing errors observed for 25m window since mitigation.

Emma (support): customer-impact check: CS dashboard shows 2 major customers saw transient increases in latency and some streaming timeouts earlier. Notifying them with a short update: "Investigating, mitigations underway, you may see reduced throughput while we shift traffic." Will prepare status.json to post to status.redwood.ai if we escalate.

Jorge (hw-ops): collected BMC logs, found fan rpm dip on node 07 before thermal hop. Opening hardware ticket to vendor for RMA for gw-west-2-accel-07 (ticket HW-2026-447). For nodes 08..10 we see elevated ECC correctable counts but stable fans; will continue monitoring.

Samira (eng-sre): monitoring metrics for 30m window. Suggest we keep nodes drained and schedule rolling reboot for 07 after offload completes. Also propose rebalancing streaming-heavy customers to dedicated pool for the next 24h.

Maya (SRE-oncall): agreed. immediate mitigation successful. Assigning follow-ups:
- Oncall handoff to Ian at 09:25PT for post-mitigation stabilization and rollback plan (if needed).
- Hardware investigation owner: Jorge (hw-ops).
- Customer comms owner: Emma (support).
- Postmortem & root cause: Ian + Samira.

Kevin (oncall): severity P1 -> lowering to P2 pending stabilization and vendor RMA acknowledgement. Recording incident timeline for postmortem.

Maya (SRE-oncall): final notes before handing off: keep nodes 07..10 drained, keep prefetch disabled on streaming for 12h, monitor p99 < 2s target. If p99 > 2s for another 15m, escalate to platform+infra leadership.

Ian (eng-runtime): taking over. I'll own postmortem and schedule follow-up runbook updates: add a step for "thermal fan dip detection -> auto-evacuate" + automated fallback to warm pool for streaming routes.

Maya (SRE-oncall): handing to Ian. thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident P1 closed -> mitigated -> severity downgraded to P2, started ticketing for postmortem (pm-2026-03-17-09).
